Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API latency SLO measurement + temporary relief request

Aisha —

Thanks for the clear asks. Per your request Im sending a concise internal playbook and a proposed temporary-relief workflow. High level first, full details + attachments to follow from Karthik: 

- Measurement: Redwood reports P50/P95 over a rolling 24h epoch with 5-minute sampling buckets. Percentiles are computed on user-visible request latencies measured at the ingress (post-auth, post-routing). Cache hits are flagged (prefix/KV), and we compute both raw and cache-excluded percentiles; the contractual commitments reference cache-excluded percentiles unless the customer opts-in to "global cache" treatment.
- Canary & Exclusion: Canary traffic is tagged and excluded from contractual windows for the first 72h after a model or infra change.
- Evidence & Audit: We can provide a time-series dump of the measurement buckets, trace IDs for sampled requests, and a signed attestation with timestamps. Standard evidence package includes the rolling 24h bucket CSV, sampling policy, and KV-cache tag legend.
- Temporary relief flow (proposed escrow): 1) Customer submits Relief Request form (sample + impact), 2) Redwood evaluates within 48h operationally and provides recommended carveout window (max 14 days without exec approval), 3) For anything >14 days or >3 repeated events in 90 days, needs VP-level signoff and PRD. Credits/rollback: limited to pro-rated usage credits tied to documented measurement deviation during the approved window.

I'm looping in Karthik (reliability) and Lauren (commercial lead) for the formal write-up and attachments. Expect the playbook + evidence checklist from Karthik in the next message.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Hosted API P50/P95 playbook + evidence checklist (attached)

Aisha, Ben —

Following Hannah's note, attached is a compact playbook and the evidence checklist. Key items (TL;DR):

1) Measurement window details
- Rolling epoch: 24h, computed every 5 minutes (non-overlapping buckets). Each bucket includes total requests, cache-hit counts, sample set sizes, and computed percentiles. We publish the aggregation script (md5) used to compute percentiles for audit reproducibility.

2) Sampling & instrumentation
- Default sampling: 100% for control plane (ingress latency) for pro-active measurement; customers can request a sampled trace dump (up to 1% of traffic for full traces).
- TTL/Cache tagging: requests served from KV or prefix caches carry X-Redwood-Cache: true. We provide both cache-included and exclude reports.

3) Canary and deployment carveouts
- Canary exclusion window is 72h post-deploy; emergency hotfixes extend exclusion up to 24h with ops approval.

4) Temporary Relief / Escrow workflow (operational steps)
- Relief request intake: customer fills form -> ops triage within 24h -> empirical review within 48h.
- Short relief (<=14 days): approved by Reliability PM + Commercial lead.
- Extended relief (>14 days): VP signoff required; limited to documented migrations or force majeure.
- Credit mechanics: calculation uses the observed delta between committed p95 and measured p95 during relief window, prorated to affected usage. Credits are capped at a percentage of monthly committed usage (standard clause).

5) Evidence package we can supply (standard):
- Rolling-bucket CSV (24h buckets)
- Aggregation script SHA256
- Sampled trace ids + anonymized traces (if requested)
- Signed attestation from Redwood Ops (timestamped)

Attachment: slo-proof-plan.pdf (includes CSV schema, aggregation script location, and sample extraction commands)

Please see the attached and call out any missing items. If Fintegrate prefers a different measurement epoch (e.g., 12h rolling), we can discuss trade-offs; that would require an amendment to the SLA language.

-Karthik
Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-proof-plan.pdf
